content.text: No audit or inspection right in the document runs against IBM as customer — every such right (§7.0, §13.1, §21.3, §24.1, Attachment 6 §4.0, Appendix A §4) is exercisable by IBM against MSL. §16.14 is a mutual record-retention obligation only and confers no verification right on MSL.

input.quote: IBM may perform process audits at MSL's or an MSL Related Company's Work Center or MSL's subcontractors' facilities to assure that identified IBM specifications have been complied with.
input.rationale: The rule targets audit/verification rights binding us as customer, and none exist in this agreement. Every audit and inspection right runs in our favour against MSL: §7.0 (IBM process audits at MSL Work Centers, with advance notice to MSL), §13.1 (IBM audit/inspection of consigned Products), §21.3 and §21.2 (IBM inspection of IBM-owned tooling), §24.1 (IBM retains the right to audit software use), Attachment 6 §4.0 (IBM monitoring/inspection/audit of MSL software installation locations, limited to MSL's business hours per p1314), and Attachment 6 Appendix A §4 (IBM/MS audit of MSL's books and records on 45 days' notice by an independent CPA, at IBM's cost unless material discrepancies, and no more frequently than semiannually). MSL is given no reciprocal right to audit or inspect IBM's books, records, facilities or systems, and there is no remote-access-to-our-systems language anywhere. §16.14 imposes only a mutual five-year record-retention obligation related to the manufacture of Products; it creates no verification or access right for MSL, so the residual burden on us is a modest recordkeeping duty rather than an audit right. Because nothing binds us, the preferred position's frequency, notice, cost and no-system-access limits are unnecessary, and no redline is warranted. Note for the file: should MSL later seek a reciprocal audit right (for example over IBM-supplied volume, consumption or pricing data), we should hold it to once per 12 months on 30 days' written notice, off-site review by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at MSL's cost unless an underpayment above 5% is found, with no direct access to our systems.
